synopsis: WorkSafe New Zealand is the national workplace-safety regulator, with an extractives inspectorate covering mines and quarries; it is distinct from WorkSafe Western Australia, which supplies the booklet’s cited Significant Incident Reports [f15673, f15674, f15681]. Its August 2017 alert followed “numerous” heavy-mobile-plant interactions, particularly involving large surface haul trucks, and illustrated ordinary-production collisions during reversing, night-shift work and stockpile loading [f3122, f3123, f3124, f3125]. For October–December 2019, its extractives vehicle- and plant-related notified events comprised 46% overturning, 27% unintended movement or brake failure, 11% collision with other plant, 4% berm breach and 12% burst tyre [f3198]. These figures describe only one quarter with acknowledged incomplete reporting, so planners should not treat them as a long-term national event distribution [f3131, f15680].
